issues.description: The code package includes ten preparation/analysis sources, but mandatory prepared inputs, local map contracts, several product producers and path/order handoffs remain unverified. The full pipeline is not closed.

The ICLINK include target is partly masked; visible consumers use home.iclink, but the supplied include identity, field contract, and local route are not established. The packaged Identifiers.csv contains only permno and cannot replace the crosswalk.

The retail and high-frequency paths rely on prepared cfrac, tclink, tclink2504 and TAQMCLINK mapping records with date/symbol keys. Their compatible sources and full contracts are not verified; the packaged identifier CSV has only permno.

The datasheet describes daily security-level aggregate FINRA volume, while stage 4 imports monthly transaction-level fields and stage 6 separately reads SS.FINRA monthly tables using date, symbol, time, shorttype and size. The stage 6 table-to-import mapping and intended product remain unresolved; the stage 4 input declarations include the field names used by stage 6.

Transcript files, the CIQ headline/date join, and precomputed call_gpt scores are not supplied or verified. The documented model vintages, consistent prompt and score range are provenance requirements; no model or API call is part of this assessment.
The outage stage requires a prepared historical event panel and a separate incident-impact CSV; their full schemas, event-time semantics, and sample coverage remain unverified.

The supplied spread program creates and exports a macro-named ret_gpt_hfbas product from four relative-spread measures; current parameters select SPL=21 and year 2021 with months 1–12. It explicitly carries both CALLSTDTTIME and TIME_ADJ_DATE into CALLS_WITH_SPREADS, but the output partition and OUT/path mapping to the eight HFIID 2021H1–2024H2 consumer tables, time semantics and value-level compatibility remain unvalidated. The separate hfrt retail input, macro-selected upstream DID_BETART input, masked call-input contract, and NBBO product also remain unresolved.

Several supplied products are produced in WORK/SCRATCH or one SAS library and consumed from another: fr_day, hfretail, hfshort, retail/short panels, and the outage high-frequency source. Stage the exact generated product before its first consumer and preserve its schema.

5_merge_call.sas imports betartonly2124_mac.dta after its earlier retail/short exports. 7_RetailAIAlign.do creates that DTA. Run SAS stage 5 through its preceding exports, then Stata stage 7, resume SAS stage 5 at the import, and only then proceed to tables.

The supplied SAS source creates DID_BETARTGPT2124_HFBAS from GPT_HFBAS and DID_TREAT and exports did_betart&ordtype.&time._hfbas.dta. Stata separately requests did_betartonly2124_hfbas.dta. Resolve macro values, destination and output-schema alignment; do not infer that the two basenames are aliases.

The 8_outage export uses macro-expanded dataset_hf and type components. The assigned dependency checklist records a Stata input name for the outage panel, but its source window is masked; confirm the exact expanded export filename and consumer before staging it.

evidence.description: Author data description sheet title.
Author-reported input families, sample universe, transcript period, model vintages, and score scale.
evidence.quote:
We obtained transcripts of conference calls from S&P Capital IQ with a data range from 2021 to 2024.

Retail trading data are from the TAQ database. Short-sale volume data are from the Financial Industry

Regulatory Authority, Inc. (FINRA), a self-regulatory organization. FINRA’s dataset includes security-

level aggregate short-sale volume data reported on a daily basis. Stock prices data including return, bid and

ask price data are obtained from the Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP). Accounting information

data are from Compustat. For intra-day bid–ask spread, we obtain it from TAQ. The dataset is confined to

common stocks listed on the NYSE, AMEX, and Nasdaq.

We generated sentiment measures from conference call transcripts using large language models provided

by OpenAI. Specifically, we used GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k for 2021–2023 transcripts and GPT-4o Mini for

2024 transcripts. The models were applied with a consistent prompt designed to classify the sentiment of

transcripts on a scale from -10 (most negative) to +10 (most positive).

review_notes: This assessment covers the full supplied pipeline only; no analysis_only path is supported by a complete compatible prepared panel and code route.
The original environment probe is opaque and is referenced only by hash. Software status comes from the pinned typed metadata viewer; SAS was never started.
All raw SAS probes are bounded one-row readability/field checks. They do not establish empirical history, full population coverage, or original author extract/vintage fidelity.
No logs, run outputs, model/API trials, SQL payloads, protected raw bodies, or source-view manifests are scientific evidence. The unverified PostgreSQL metadata artifact was not cited.

The approved source viewer masked credential/path tokens and some block-comment rows. In particular the table-code outage use-site window around line 696 is masked; D0128 is retained as a checklist-linked issue and not quoted as visible source.
The D0123 SAS output uses ordtype/time macro components and is not assumed equal to the fixed Stata filename. The D0128 outage export/consumer basename also needs explicit confirmation.

Exact catalog lookup misses for TAQ CTM, NBBO, TAQMCLINK and FINRA do not establish unavailable data or licensing barriers. The FINRA public notice distinguishes monthly transaction-detail files from daily aggregates.
The 5_merge_call / 7_RetailAIAlign interleave is source-proven. Stage 5 outputs first, run stage 7, resume stage 5 at the import, then run table code.
